CANDIDATE bd-01M158KA75HGGM118P3SQ1RHYK items (2)-(4): 1eb0fa9 on worktree-agent-a32866200333a2f5c, parent 414070a (main; descendant of the landed AlignWire e780f12). Four reserved paths only, +240/-16: align/population.scala, align/PopulationSuite.scala, laws/Laws.scala, laws/LawsSuite.scala. Reservations rv-01M15N5EXR4N30AMP3GNG2DEZ5 (align) and rv-01M15NAMEK9PV57FZDNSF46Y9F (laws). Not merged.

(2) PopulationAggregate.of refuses a proof whose viewFingerprint is not the aggregate view's contentFingerprint, and a subject whose recallChecksum is not AlignWire.recallChecksum of the recall it carries. Both checks run BEFORE the unknown-node and malformed-row scans, because a proof from a look-alike view would otherwise pass the node scan whenever its anchors happen to exist here - the fingerprint is the thing that refuses it, and a test pins that ordering.

ERROR SHAPE: AlignError.FingerprintMismatch(field, recorded, derived) - the case the wire slice introduced - with the field carrying the subject id: "viewFingerprint (subject s-foreign)" / "recallChecksum (subject s-wrong)". Recorded is the value the proof carries, derived is what this view/recall gives, both as hex. I chose FingerprintMismatch over InconsistentResult so the population failure is the same typed thing the decoder's AlignWire.matched reports, and a consumer can pattern-match one case for "this proof does not belong to this model" wherever it arises. The subject id rides in the field string because the case has no subject slot and I did not want to widen a just-landed public error type for it; if the chief prefers a dedicated case or a subject-carrying variant, say so and I will change it in a follow-up rather than churn the wire error now.

API CHANGE: SubjectAlignment gains recall: RecallGraph (subject, recall, result, wordCount). It is the only way to check that a proof was made from the transcript the subject is presented with. No in-repo call site outside population.scala/PopulationSuite constructs it (the sole other mention is a Scaladoc reference in hsmm.scala:132), so nothing else needed changing; downstream population code that constructs subjects must add the recall.

(3) PopulationReceipt(viewFingerprint, subjectCount, recallChecksums sorted by hex) on PopulationAggregate.receipt, so a population artifact names the one view every proof was gated against and the transcripts pooled, independent of subject order.

(4) Tests and law. PopulationSuite gains: the foil - a view with the SAME node ids and one lemma added to e1, two real inferences from GraphHsmm.infer, aggregate over the wrong view is Left with the view field and the subject named, each proof aggregates on its own view, and the foil aggregate's receipt is bound to the foil fingerprint; the check-ordering test; a wrong-recall subject refused; the receipt contents; and receipt/aggregate invariance under subject order. New PopulationLaws (laws.population, registered in LawsSuite) with five rules over generated cases: own-view proofs accepted with a view-bound receipt; every fingerprintVariants same-view variant accepted and every different-content variant refused (same node ids included); a mixed population succeeds iff every subject matches, naming the offending subject; a unit-text-only recall change refused; receipt invariant under subject order.

EVIDENCE at 1eb0fa9, clean pin 0329c43: scalafmtCheckAll green; alignJVM 125/125, alignJS 125/125, alignNative 125/125 (was 120 - five new tests); lawsJVM 81/81 (was 76 - five new rules). INCOMPLETE, and I am flagging it rather than papering over it: fixturesJVM and interviewJVM did NOT run - sbt died in dependency resolution with java.io.IOException: No space left on device. The machine's disk is at 100% (926Gi total, 867Gi used, 96Mi free), which is a workspace-wide condition, not something this change caused and not something I will fix by deleting other sessions' files. Neither module constructs SubjectAlignment or PopulationAggregate (whole-repo grep: only a Scaladoc mention in hsmm.scala), so the risk from the missing legs is compile-level only, but that is an argument, not evidence - please re-run those two legs in the archive gate once there is disk, and treat this candidate as unlanded until then.

Item (5), codec decodes only against the matching model, stays with codex-storymodel4s-root in the HsmmResultCodec slice; the decoder already calls AlignWire.matched, which is the same check at the wire boundary.
